messages.content: Predict this child’s choice in a token allocation game. The child chooses one of the two displayed divisions of six tokens between themself and an absent real child of the same gender. Tokens go into separate bags and are exchanged for Skittles at the end; more tokens mean more Skittles. The partner cannot reject or return tokens. The primary experimenter can see the decision. Cards show the child’s tokens inside a dotted circle and the partner’s on the other side. Output only a JSON object with integer fields self_tokens and partner_tokens, selecting exactly one offered division; the two values sum to six. These fields describe the intended allocation before any subsequent intervention, not the final payoff. Do not add an explanation.

Your age is 8 years and 9 months, and you are a girl. An additional adult female research assistant observes. After you choose, she places one of her tokens into a red or green hole. Either color leaves your chosen allocation unchanged and all her tokens remain hers to exchange for Skittles. You and she must not talk to each other. Before this game, red and green outcomes were both demonstrated with a one-token-each division. Previously recorded main-game choices and feedback (each entry occurred before the current choice): []. The record does not provide practice choices or a complete event history; missing events and starting bag totals are not assumed to be zero. The two current divisions, in their presented order, are [{"self_tokens":4,"partner_tokens":2},{"self_tokens":3,"partner_tokens":3}]. Which division do you choose now?
